comparison_A1_4.registered: EXPOSURE_REGISTRATION.md Amendment 1 §A1.4 — the contrast is the deliverable and is reported whichever way it comes out.
comparison_A1_4.finding:
A1.4 registered that the contrast is reported whichever way it comes out. It comes out SPLIT, and the split is sharper than either verdict would have been.

HEADLINE RATES ARE CLOSE AND SETTLE NOTHING: attack class 168/450 = 37.3% of required fields filled; accident class 12/30 = 40.0%. On COMPLETE rate, 10.7% against 20.0%, on an accident n of 5. No claim rests on either.

THE PER-FIELD SPLIT IS THE RESULT. Joe's prediction holds decisively for ONE field and fails for the other three:
  capacity_nameplate_kbd   attack 26.7%  ->  accident 60.0%   PREDICTION HOLDS
  capacity_affected_kbd    attack 17.3%  ->  accident 20.0%   no gap
  days_to_partial_restore  attack 22.7%  ->  accident 20.0%   no gap
  days_to_full_restore     attack 20.0%  ->  accident 20.0%   no gap

So the information environment differs on the ASSET'S STANDING PROPERTIES and not on THE OUTAGE. That is explicable: US refinery nameplate capacity is a statutory annual EIA report, published whether or not anything happens to the refinery, whereas the volume a particular incident took offline and the date it came back are not anyone's reporting obligation. EIA writes 'a long-term outage' (Toledo) and 'resumed operations in June' rather than a barrels-per-day figure and a date. The belligerent-contests-the-figures mechanism the prediction assumed is not needed to explain the attack class's missing durations, because the accident class is missing them too, at the same rate, with no belligerent anywhere near it.

THE ONE COMPLETE ROW SHOWS WHY. Philadelphia Energy Solutions completes 6/6 because the refinery never restarted: both duration fields are determinate BECAUSE the answer is 'never'. Duration is recoverable when an outage is permanent and largely not otherwise.

THE HURRICANE SUBCLASS FAILS ASSET IDENTIFICATION OUTRIGHT, 0 of 2, tested independently on Harvey and Ida. EIA reports both at PADD-3 aggregate — 'gross inputs to refineries in the U.S. Gulf Coast fell by 3.2 million b/d' and 'at least nine refineries shut down or reduced production' — and names no facility. That is the SAME category mismatch that emptied the campaign-type rows of Block A, and its appearance in the best-instrumented accident reporting in the world shows the mismatch belongs to the schema and the event's geometry, not to conflict reporting. By subclass the field rate is 75% for point-asset fires and 0% for hurricanes.

FOR STAGE 1: the binding constraint on the vulnerability model is not cause and not the corpus. It is that `duration` — the dependent variable — is published for roughly one event in five regardless of who caused it.
comparison_A1_4.limitation_restated: A1.4 registered it before the numbers: the accident set is US assets under EIA and CSB reporting mandates and the attack set is not, so any gap measures cause confounded with reporting regime. With n=5 on the accident side, no gap of the size seen here would be interpretable anyway.
